faq_heading: Surrey market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Surrey in 3 parts: Surrey (board area), North Surrey and Cloverdale. In September 2026, Cloverdale had the highest all-home benchmark at $921,900 and North Surrey the lowest at $639,100, a gap of $282,800. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Surrey (board area) down 7.0%, North Surrey down 8.8%, Cloverdale down 5.8%.
Surrey (board area) benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical Surrey (board area) home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $906,200 in September 2026. That is little changed at −0.7% on the month, down 1.8% over three months, down 4.2% over six months and down 7.0% over the year. Over three years it is down 18.8%, and over five years down 10.7%.
The weakest one-year move in Surrey (board area) was for an apartment homes at −11.5%; the strongest was a townhouse at −3.9%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,304,100) and an apartment ($460,200) is $843,900, and a townhouse ($749,600) sits $289,400 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $861,300, Surrey (board area) is 5.2% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 7.2% against down 7.0% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, Surrey (board area) ranks 5 by all-home benchmark, with Cloverdale above it at $921,900 and Mission below it at $797,500.

Detached homes in Surrey (board area): benchmark $1,304,100, little changed at −1.4% in a month, down 2.5% in three months, down 4.9% in six months, down 9.0% in a year, down 17.5% in three years and down 8.0% in five. That is 0.3% above the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,300,000).

Townhouse homes in Surrey (board area): benchmark $749,600, little changed at +0.2% in a month, little changed at −1.1% in three months, down 3.0% in six months, down 3.9% in a year, down 12.4% in three years and up 1.7% in five. That is 0.6% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($745,300).

Apartment homes in Surrey (board area): benchmark $460,200, little changed at −0.6% in a month, down 4.5% in three months, down 6.8% in six months, down 11.5% in a year, down 16.7% in three years and up 4.2% in five. That is 0.3% below the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($461,800).

blocks.text: North Surrey benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical North Surrey home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $639,100 in September 2026. That is little changed at −0.3% on the month, little changed at −1.1% over three months, down 4.6% over six months and down 8.8% over the year. Over three years it is down 20.1%, and over five years down 16.6%.
The weakest one-year move in North Surrey was for a detached home homes at −10.9%; the strongest was a townhouse at −8.1%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,252,600) and an apartment ($398,900) is $853,700, and a townhouse ($680,400) sits $281,500 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $861,300, North Surrey is 25.8% below. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 7.2% against down 8.8% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, North Surrey ranks 8 by all-home benchmark, with Abbotsford above it at $701,900.

Detached homes in North Surrey: benchmark $1,252,600, little changed at −0.8% in a month, down 2.0% in three months, down 6.8% in six months, down 10.9% in a year, down 16.1% in three years and down 10.3% in five. That is 3.6% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,300,000).

Townhouse homes in North Surrey: benchmark $680,400, little changed at −0.2% in a month, down 1.8% in three months, little changed at −0.8% in six months, down 8.1% in a year, down 11.1% in three years and up 4.2% in five. That is 8.7% below the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($745,300).

Apartment homes in North Surrey: benchmark $398,900, little changed at −0.6% in a month, down 2.5% in three months, down 6.6% in six months, down 10.4% in a year, down 19.3% in three years and down 6.0% in five. That is 13.6% below the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($461,800).

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Surrey?
faq.a: In September 2026, a typical Surrey (board area) home was $906,200, with detached at $1,304,100. In September 2026, a typical North Surrey home was $639,100, with detached at $1,252,600. In September 2026, a typical Cloverdale home was $921,900, with detached at $1,317,200.

faq.q: Are Surrey home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Surrey (board area) is down 7.0% over twelve months and down 1.8% over three months. North Surrey is down 8.8% over twelve months and little changed at −1.1% over three months. Cloverdale is down 5.8% over twelve months and down 2.5% over three months.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.
